name: Shawi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Rojas-Berscia, Luis Miguel. 2019. From Kawapanan to Shawi: Topics in language variation and change. PhD dissertation, Radboud Universiteit Nijmegen, iv+529 pp. hdl:2066/204333 (open copy on MPG PuRe)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: §3.4 Phonology (pp. 52-63: 3.4.1 Phonemes, 3.4.2 Syllable structure, 3.4.3 Processes) is the same material as the JIPA Illustration. Keywords carry stress marks (p. 53: 'Keywords are offered in phonemic transcription with syllable boundaries indicated by dots and stress by [ˈ]', e.g. ˈpa.nɘn 'hill', ka.ˈna.ɾan 'type of otter', ma.ˈna.pa.ɾa 'ring'), but there is no statement of where stress falls and no stress/prosody subsection anywhere in the table of contents.

sources.citation: Rojas Berscia, Luis Miguel. 2013. La sintaxis y semántica de las construcciones causativas en el chayahuita de Balsapuerto. Tesis, Pontificia Universidad Católica del Perú. 121 pp. hdl:20.500.12404/4670
sources.note: §3.3.3 Rasgos suprasegmentales (p. 30): 'Los rasgos suprasegmentales en la lengua chayahuita son: la duración, la aspiración, la glotalización y la nasalización', quoting Hart et al. 1976: 3 who treat these four as 'covocales'. Stress/acento is not listed or mentioned; the author explicitly defers a new phonological analysis ('no planeamos dar mayor detalle sobre este aspecto de la lengua').

sources.citation: Rojas-Berscia, Luis Miguel, Andrés Napurí & Lei Wang. 2020 [online 2019]. Shawi (Chayahuita). Illustrations of the IPA. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 50(3): 417-430. doi:10.1017/S0025100318000415
sources.note: Marks primary stress [ˈ] on every keyword (p. 419: 'syllable boundaries indicated by dots and stress by [ˈ]'), with stress on the first syllable in some words (ˈsa.na.pi 'woman', ˈna.ni 'already', ˈtaʃiʔ 'night') and on the second in others (ni.ˈto.ton 'intelligent', kan.ˈpi.ta 2PL, na.ˈɾi 'joke', a.ˈma.ʃa 'a bit', wa.ˈɾan.ka 'thousand'); but the Illustration has NO stress section — sections are Consonants, Vowels, Syllable structure, Processes. Footnote 5 (p. 422) says 'We are not marking the primary stress in this word because of its complex morphosyntactic nature. More on this phenomenon c…

sources.citation: Barraza de García, Yris Julia. 2005. El sistema verbal en la lengua Shawi. Tesis de doctorado, Universidade Federal de Pernambuco, Recife. 220 pp.
sources.note: Ch. III 'Breve análisis fonológico' (pp. 37-63): phoneme inventory (incl. /h/ as phoneme), syllable (C)V(C), distribution, processes (voicing from the third syllable leftwards, etc.). No stress statement; the word 'acento' does not occur; p. 12 states 'nos falta profundizar los estudios sobre los rasgos suprasegmentales'.
Nothing on stress; phonology tables sourced from Rojas-Berscia 2019 and Barraza 2005.

sources.citation: Hart, Helen (comp.). 1988 [2nd ed. 2008]. Diccionario chayahuita-castellano (Canponanquë nisha nisha nonacaso'). Serie Lingüística Peruana 29. Lima: Ministerio de Educación / Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. 495 pp.
sources.note: No word-stress rule. p. 13 (Ortografía): 'Se emplea el acento ortográfico para indicar énfasis o intensidad' — the written accent marks emphasis, not lexical stress. p. 290 (Notas gramaticales §10.1.5 El vocativo y el énfasis): emphasis is produced 'con mayor fuerza de voz y agregando a la vocal acentuada un sonido parecido al de la j castellana', written with an acute on the 'sílaba acentuada'. The Guía de pronunciación (p. 14) discusses voicing 'después de la segunda sílaba', nasalisation and syncope but not stress.

sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Shawi; every later description cites it. Its treatment of suprasegmentals ('covocales': length, aspiration, glottalisation, nasalisation) is the place a statement on accent/stress (or its absence) would be made. SIL has digitised the DEL series ( for DEL 7 at sil.org/resources/archives/30014), so a probably exists under an entry number that the bot-blocked search page hides.
